findings.title: Login cache is not invalidated when an IDP in a disabled organization is updated
findings.body:
`update()` reads `original` through `this.getById` (line 91). When the ORGANIZATION feature is on, that returns the org-aware wrapper, and its `isEnabled()` returns false whenever the linked organization is disabled (lines 434-444). The cached ID set, though, comes from `idpDelegate.getForLogin`, and the JPA query only filters on the IDP's own `enabled` column (JPAIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:234-238). It ignores the organization's state. So an IDP that is enabled, public and linked to a disabled org is in the cached ORG_ONLY/ALL lists, while `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` returns false.

Here is how it fails. Org A is disabled, and IDP X (enabled, public, linked to A) is in the cached login list. An admin sets `hideOnLogin=true`, or removes `BROKER_PUBLIC`, or sets link-only. The admin REST path builds a fresh, unwrapped model (IdentityProviderResource.java:191,197), so the predicate on `updated` is also false. The early return at line 405 skips the invalidation. When org A is enabled again, the cached path re-reads X by id (line 246). The bean then re-checks only `isEnabled()` (OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:75,80), so X shows on the login page even though it is hidden, link-only or not public. Nothing logs or reports this.

Fix: evaluate the predicate on the raw stored model (`idpDelegate.getById(...)`) instead of the wrapper. Or make the invalidation decision with the same per-IDP fields the JPA query uses (enabled, linkOnly, hideOnLogin, organizationId, BROKER_PUBLIC), not the org-aware `isEnabled()`. The new test never disables the organization, so it does not cover this case.

findings.title: Cleanup removes the literal alias "alias", not the created IDPs
findings.body: `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` registers a removal of an IDP named `alias`, which does not exist. The 21 IDPs created here (`idp-alias-0` … `idp-alias-20`) are never cleaned up. The same mistake is at line 425, and it copies the existing pattern at line 303. Use `get(idpRep.getAlias())`, capturing the alias in a local variable inside the loop.

contracts.action: getForLogin now serves the IDP list from a per-realm, per-FetchMode cache keyed by organizationId
contracts.equivalent_path: getByOrganization (same file, lines 168-211) uses the same IdentityProviderListQuery pattern
contracts.before_after: Same structure as getByOrganization: bypass the cache if the key is invalid, build or extend the query, then resolve the IDs through session.identityProviders().getById, falling back to the delegate on a miss. getByOrganization also bypasses when the orgId itself is invalid; getForLogin has no org-level check, and relies on the bean re-checking isEnabled for org enable/disable.
contracts.visible_effect: The login page IDP buttons come from these results through OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders and IdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders. Those only re-check isEnabled and alias; they do not re-check hideOnLogin, linkOnly or BROKER_PUBLIC, so a stale ID set shows up directly on the page.
contracts.failure_mode: A missed invalidation leaves IDPs on the login page that should be hidden (see the finding on line 405).

contracts.action: Login-cache invalidation on IDP create/update/remove, and on org link/unlink (which goes through update)
contracts.equivalent_path: JpaOrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider change the orgId and call session.identityProviders().update
contracts.before_after: Org link and unlink go through update(), so a change in orgId triggers invalidation. The 'original' model is the org-aware wrapper, while the cached set comes from the JPA filter on the raw enabled column. The two disagree when the org is disabled.
contracts.visible_effect: A stale login list after an update while the org is disabled.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent: no error, and the wrong IDP buttons are shown.

contracts.action: getLoginPredicate now also requires org-linked IDPs to be BROKER_PUBLIC
contracts.equivalent_path: The default getForLogin adds BROKER_PUBLIC=true for org IDPs (lines 173-181)
contracts.before_after: The predicate now matches the getForLogin search semantics. It is also used by IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so linked non-public org IDPs are now dropped from the federated-identity list in the base bean as well.
contracts.visible_effect: Users with a federated identity from a non-public org IDP no longer see that IDP through the base IdentityProviderBean.

summary: The PR caches `getForLogin` results per realm and fetch mode, invalidates the cache on IDP create/update/remove, and re-checks the org-aware `isEnabled` in the bean. One bug: `update()` decides whether to invalidate by testing the org-aware wrapper. When the IDP's organization is disabled, that wrapper reports the IDP as disabled, while the cached list is built from the raw JPA `enabled` column. So updates such as hide-on-login, link-only or removing broker-public are not invalidated while the org is disabled. Once the org is re-enabled, the stale entry shows on the login page. Separately, the new test's cleanup removes a literal `\"alias\"` instead of the IDPs it created.
